newsitem.title: CHINA: China hands down sentences in $184 million scandal.
newsitem.headline: China hands down sentences in $184 million scandal.

text.p: China has handed down sentences ranging from jail to death to a group of officials ensnared in banking scandals involving more than 1.53 billion yuan ($184 million), the Economic Information Daily said on Monday.

Several officials from a branch of the Communications Bank of China in Suzhou in eastern Jiangsu province had been found guilty of taking bribes for handing out billions of yuan in illegal loans, the newspaper said.

From 1990 to 1993, the bank's general manager Cai Hangang and other bank officials had made the loans to "lawless persons" from companies in Beijing, southern Hainan island, the southern boomtown of Shenzhen, northeastern Harbin and elsewhere, the newspaper said.
An investigation by the Suzhou Intermediate Court had found that of the 1.53 billion yuan in loans, some 840 million yuan was now overdue and would be difficult to recover, it said.

General manager Cai, management committee director Yang Hesheng and planning department director Ge Xiaofei had taken millions of yuan worth of bribes, embezzled bank money and misused public funds, the newspaper said.

The court sentenced Yang to 10 years in prison for taking bribes and neglect of duty while Ge was given a two-year suspended death sentence for taking bribes and for embezzlement, it said. A suspended death sentence can be commuted to life in prison if the prisoner shows a good attitude.
Zhu Daming, Ge's husband and general manager of the Suzhou Xinyi Group Co, was given life in prison for embezzlement and bribery, the newspaper said.
Cai had died of a brain haemorrhage while in custody, it said but gave no further details.

Beijing, worried that growing public dissatisfaction with official graft could threaten its grip on power, has launched several anti-corruption campaigns in recent months, but many residents complain the results have been patchy at best.
